findings.claim: The learning/control support is the score-clock window [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score nodes; the objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only.

For landmark_00_local_dx the observed curve is non-monotone across the window: it rises to a positive peak near the middle of the window, then falls to a negative trough, then partially recovers toward zero by the last node. The whole-window mean is near zero, so the endpoint contrast is small relative to the within-window excursion.

The continuous-trend summary for landmark_00_local_dx reports a strongly negative first-node rate and a strongly positive last-node rate with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches; the quadratic polynomial is not accepted and extrapolation is not allowed. This is consistent with a changing, non-stationary contrast rather than a stable linear drift.

hypotheses.direction: time-dependent rather than constant; no absolute target value is specified by the contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: If the per-node curve for landmark_00_local_dx is reproduced as monotone or as a stable single-sign contrast across independent batches, the time-dependent hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.scope: all seeds over the full observed score-clock window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate contrast changes sign within the observed window, so a single fixed endpoint target for this coordinate is not supported by the observed curve; a time-dependent treatment of this coordinate is the candidate worth testing.

hypotheses.direction: schedule should follow the observed contrast shape rather than a constant value
hypotheses.falsifier: If the observed curve is flat within batch noise or the whole-window mean equals the mid-window excursion, the schedule hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx whole-window mean versus within-window excursion
hypotheses.scope: all seeds over the full observed window
hypotheses.statement: Because the whole-window mean of landmark_00_local_dx is near zero while the within-window excursion is large, an endpoint-only reward on this coordinate would under-represent the observed mid-window contrast; a smooth schedule that tracks the observed contrast is the candidate to test at fixed dose.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves and summary tables were read.
The curve is a coordinate proxy in predicted endpoint world coordinates; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
Selection preference and survival are not established as final affinity benefit; no decoded final-affinity labels were observed.
Only one feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read in full; other landmark coordinates were not individually inspected.
The quadratic polynomial was not accepted and extrapolation is disallowed, so no statement is made outside [0.0, 0.49].
